query_text: Why do men have larger Adam's apples?

content.text:
Men tend to have larger **Adam’s apples** because of how the **larynx**, or voice box, changes during puberty.

The Adam’s apple is the visible bump made by the **thyroid cartilage**, which surrounds the larynx. During puberty, **testosterone** causes the male larynx to grow more than it typically does in females. As the larynx enlarges, the thyroid cartilage protrudes farther forward in the neck, making the Adam’s apple more noticeable.

This growth also lengthens and thickens the vocal cords, which is why many boys’ voices become deeper during puberty.

Women also have thyroid cartilage and therefore technically have an Adam’s apple too, but it is usually smaller and less prominent because the larynx generally grows less during puberty.
